analyst.summary: Motilal Oswal posted a record FY26 with core operating profit up 16% (Q4 up 25%), powered by its asset-management and wealth-management arms, which are growing AUM 30%+ a year and now generate more than three-quarters of group revenue — a real, multi-year shift away from pure stock-broking. Two things temper the story: quarterly headline profit is noisy because a large in-house investment book gets marked to market every quarter (it swung a Rs 661 cr operating profit quarter into a reported loss in Q4), and the broking/capital-markets piece still faces SEBI's ongoing derivatives-curb agenda, though full-service brokers like Motilal Oswal are expected to feel it far less than discount brokers. At roughly 24-28x FY26 earnings, the stock looks fairly priced for a successful continued shift to annuity revenue, not cheap enough to be a clear buy-the-dip and not troubled enough to sell. Hold.
